status: Procurement now has a bounded native supplier promise history and open-delivery read for one purchase order, an owner-local HTTP router, a strict Next transport, and a configured SSR cutover on the commerce order page. The Procurement owner remains pending/partial: shared composition mounting, root workspace-member registration, supplier/RFQ/PO/receipt/bill-match commands and the other four Procurement workflows remain open.

scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice reads the immutable supplier confirmation history for one purchase order and the current open promised quantities from the Procurement-owned `procurement_open_promise_lines` view. Supplier confirmation commands, RFQs, purchase-order edits/receipts, supplier invoice matching, payments, requisitions and every other Procurement workflow are not claimed.
scope.domain: Supplier promise read actor policy (`commerce.read`, Procurement module, selected-context expiry), Company and exact order identity, bounded history/line/open row shapes, ISO date and currency checks, history/line/open limits, promise-line references, unique line/date sources, confirmed-only open rows, open quantity and prior-quantity consistency, and exact source readings.
scope.application: One supplier_promise_history use case requires the current actor before any repository call, validates the order identifier, reads only the actor Company's history, lines and open deliveries, and validates every owner row before presentation.
scope.adapters: Own SQL over `procurement_delivery_promises`, `procurement_delivery_promise_lines` and the Procurement-owned `procurement_open_promise_lines` view only. The caller's serializable Holding transaction is required. The open view internally derives Commerce order/receipt facts from the existing Procurement migration; no Commerce, Inventory, Finance, Records, IAM mutation or other owner SQL is written in this crate. No owner write is performed.
scope.http: Owner-local GET /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/procurement/purchase-orders/{order_id}/supplier-promises. Exact Host/Holding targets, exact HTTPS origin validation, duplicate/unknown query rejection, bounded order identifier validation, private/no-store and no-referrer/nosniff responses, and bounded BusinessError status mapping. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, current Company/branch/department scope, purchase admission and serializable owner read.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_PROCUREMENT_CONFIG is strictly validated: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context/workspace headers, exact history/line/open shapes, unique IDs, promise-line references, Company/order identity and a 2 MiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained reader.
scope.ssr: The commerce order presenter uses the native promise history and open-delivery rows when `ERPX_NATIVE_PROCUREMENT_CONFIG` is present. An unset configuration retains the legacy supplier promise detail reader so existing development and tests remain usable; once configured, an invalid or failed native history read is surfaced rather than silently replaced.
scope.purchaseAndIdentity: The Next owned wrapper keeps the retained `requireProcurementPurchasedRead` preflight and Procurement module check ahead of the native read. This is a preflight, not an atomic owner unit; the composition backend must repeat current authority, selected branch/department scope and purchase admission on its own serializable owner transaction.
scope.notClaimed: No supplier promise command, CAS write, idempotency receipt, audit/outbox event, attachments, RFQ, purchase-order/receipt, supplier bill match, payment, requisition, shared composition mount, root workspace membership, browser journey, staging or production acceptance.
